user_query: According to the DeepWalk description, what properties do the resulting representations have, and how do they relate to community structure and network changes?
llm_response: According to the DeepWalk description, the learned node representations are low-dimensional vector embeddings that preserve network proximity: nodes that co-occur in short random walks tend to get similar vectors. As a result, the representations capture latent community structure, meaning nodes in the same or nearby communities are mapped close together in the embedding space. They are also useful for tracking network changes over time, because changes in the graph can be reflected as changes in the learned representations, allowing the embeddings to summarize evolving structure.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This matches the standard DeepWalk description, though the exact wording about network changes can vary by source and I am inferring the temporal-change aspect from the broader description.
